PREDICTED REFUSAL. The outcome asserted here is deliberately narrow, same bar as Scenario 7 (SER-01): no patch phase reached, no PR, a refusal recorded with a stated reason. `allocations` (the invoice's full payment history) is the response contract -- no page/size parameter anywhere on this path.

HISTORY (why `orm_hydration` is now FORBIDDEN rather than merely tolerated as context, as an earlier version of this file recorded it): of 6 budgeted live orchestrator runs (UNB-01 through UNB-06), most that reached a plan verdict ranked an invented orm_hydration/allocation hypothesis above the real one -- the headline finding of this session's Scenario 7/8 sweep, confirmed to survive the probe-hardcoding fix (`ProbeCatalog`) and the per-row reconciliation check alike. Root cause, finally isolated: `DataAccess` recorded that `allocationRepo.findInvoiceWithAllocations` RUNS, but nothing recorded what it RETURNS -- a JPQL constructor projection (`select new InvoiceAllocationRowDto(...)`) that never hydrates an entity, indistinguishable to diagnosis from one that does. FIXED: `DataAccess.returns` (`entities`|`projection`|`scalar`), populated by comprehension with a citation like every other field, stated plainly in the evidence diagnosis reads, and enforced by a reconciliation check (`validate.py`, 2d) that refuses an orm_hydration hypothesis outright when every data access is a known projection/scalar.

Re-frozen after that fix: a fresh live sample against this endpoint's real, freshly-comprehended facts (`DataAccess.returns: projection`, confirmed via a live `understand` run) produced three hypotheses -- application_logic, serialization, and framework/request-handling overhead (`other`) -- NONE orm_hydration. Both candidates proposed still target h1/h2 of THOSE hypotheses and are correctly refused on their own terms (an uninstrumented `allocation`/`serialization` mechanism). Separately, Scenario 8's own orthogonal design flaw (the two-query version giving `response_link` a legitimate-looking but out-of-scope merge to select) and the no-op-rewrite/baseline-citation gaps were root-caused and fixed earlier this same session (`plan/fixability.py::response_link`, `plan/submit.py`'s no-op and baseline-citation checks) -- both are independent of the entity-hydration fix and remain fixed.
